What is a nebula?
a: A cloud of dust and gas from which stars form.

q: What starts a star shining?
a: Gravity pulls gas together until fusion starts.

q: Why is a main sequence star stable?
a: Gravity inwards is balanced by the outward push from fusion.

q: Stages of a star like the Sun?
a: Nebula, main sequence, red giant, white dwarf.

q: Why does a star become a red giant?
a: Hydrogen runs low; it swells and its surface cools, so it glows red.

q: What is a white dwarf?
a: A small, hot, dense core left when the outer layers drift away.

q: Stages of a star much larger than the Sun?
a: Nebula, main sequence, red supergiant, supernova, neutron star (or black hole).

q: What is a supernova?
a: An explosion of a massive star that throws dust and gas into space.

q: What is left after a supernova?
a: A neutron star (or a black hole for the most massive stars).

q: Will the Sun become a supernova?
a: No. It will become a red giant, then a white dwarf.

q: What is apparent brightness?
a: How bright a star looks from Earth; it depends on distance.

q: What is absolute magnitude?
a: The brightness of a star at a standard distance.

q: Why use absolute magnitude?
a: It removes the effect of distance so stars can be compared fairly.

Property directly related to surface temperature? (J25)
What is the Big Bang theory?
a: The universe began from one tiny, hot, dense place and has expanded and cooled since.

q: What happened to the universe as it expanded?
a: It cooled, and gravity formed stars and galaxies.

q: What is the Doppler effect?
a: A change in observed frequency and wavelength when a wave source moves relative to an observer.

q: Source moving towards you: what happens?
a: Shorter wavelength, higher frequency (blue-shift for light).

q: Source moving away from you: what happens?
a: Longer wavelength, lower frequency (red-shift for light).

q: Two pieces of evidence for the Big Bang? (J25)
a: CMB radiation and red-shift of galaxies.

q: What is the CMB?
a: Microwaves from all directions: the afterglow of the Big Bang.

q: Why is the CMB wavelength longer now? (J25)
a: Its wavelength has increased because the universe is expanding.
